aboutMore: things that are not the band (there are 4): i work weekends at the dairy queen. i can make a blizzard in 14 seconds and have only ever flipped one upside down for a kid, with permission. the ice cream machine is down about half the time, which is the most garage band thing about the job. my paychecks go to guitar strings, sharpies, and CD-Rs (the sharpies are the biggest line). my dad (extension cord exception) fixed our amp with a soldering iron in 20 minutes and has never brought it up. my mom says i have 'a lot of drive.' i say it's mostly the bike.

blog.title: DAD'S RULES: the complete list (v4)
blog.body: 1. done by 8:15. 2. the extension cord stays under the door mat so nobody trips (the cord is the exception, see: every other rule). 3. nobody touches the dryer, it's a drum riser. 4. garage door up for air, down at 8:15. 5. nobody sits on the lawn mower, it is not a stage. 6. if a neighbor complains, the band is 'working on it.' 7. no fire. 8. no strobe lights. (yes there was a strobe light.) 9. every band that plays gets a note on the fridge: 'good job. -Dad.' (evan asked to keep his. it was his first.) 10. everybody eats something before they play. 11. the gas can stays on the shelf. 12. the dad may request one (1) song. 13. a kitchen timer is set for however long the band gets (ember got 9 minutes). at 8:14 the dad comes to the door and says 'one more.' 14. he has requested the same song for four months: Voltage Heart. he says it's 'because it goes hard.' he says it like an engineering review. i never told the band. i'm telling the blog. v5 coming soon.

blog.title: i found out who wrote 'please' (a mystery with a baby in it)
blog.body: so the note on my garage door. the one that just says 'please.' i took it across the street. it was the pattersons. they have a baby named june. she is 3 weeks old. she naps from 6 to 8. we start at 7. mr. patterson was very nice about it. he said 'we love it, we just need her to sleep through the first half.' i said sorry about 14 times. he said 'it's fine, it's a good band' and i almost sat down on his lawn. so on friday we turned the amp around, played at a whisper, and did the whole set on one amp at 2. we're calling it the lullaby set. june slept through everything except the bridge of Fractured Signal (7/8, nobody sleeps through that). afterward mr. patterson took the note back, wrote 'thank you' under 'please,' and taped it up again. it's on the garage door now. i'm not taking it down.

blog.title: how i write a song (a process) (it starts with the dishwasher)
blog.body: step 1: i carry a dictation recorder (it was my dad's, it's the size of a candy bar) and i hum into it whenever an idea shows up. i have 41 memos. 6 are riffs. 5 are me saying 'remember this.' 1 is the dishwasher (about halfway through the cycle it goes da-da-DUM da and i'm convinced it's a bridge). step 2: play it on guitar until it sounds like a song. step 3: bring it to practice, bryan says 'sick' (not a yes, not a no). step 4: lucas writes words on the back of a receipt. step 5: we play it so many times i can't tell if it's good. step 6: we play it for chad. chad cheers. it's good. Voltage Heart started on a school bus. you can hear the bus on the memo. you can hear a girl say 'ugh, stop.' that's the first take. i kept it. working titles for the next one: 'Dial Tone Heart' and 'Parking Lot Anthem.' nobody has voted. lucas wants it to be about the rake again.

blog.title: WEEKEND AT THE DQ (a log of what people say through a speaker)
blog.body: things said to me through the drive-thru speaker this weekend. 1) 'one of those, with the candy.' (a blizzard. i knew.) 2) 'is the machine up?' (no.) 3) 'what do u mean no?' (i said it's resting. he said ok. he was very understanding.) 4) a kid in the back seat asked if i'm in a band. i said yes. he said 'what's it called.' i said STATIC PROPHECY. he said 'is it good?' i said 'it goes hard.' he said 'ok, 2 cones.' that's the best review we've gotten and he paid for it. 5) chad orders a large chocolate cone every saturday and says 'GREAT SERVICE' into the speaker. he's the only one who says it. i've never told him it's just a speaker. the real budget of STATIC PROPHECY: $97 a week, 14 hours of blizzards. strings, sharpies, CD-Rs. the band is a savings account with a garage.

survey.title: the BAND survey (every band does one) (we did it on index cards)
qa: band name:
STATIC PROPHECY. it was the static between two stations on the garage radio. the 'prophecy' part was lucas
formed:
march. in my garage. 2 people and a cooler
genre:
pop-punk but it has feelings. lucas says 'emo.' bryan says 'sick.' chad says 'rock.' the neighbors say 'please'
how many songs:
6 now. Voltage Heart, Circuit Breaker, Fractured Signal, Rake Incident, and a couple that don't have a name yet. #6 is called 'Extension Cord.' it's a love song to a rule
biggest crowd:
23 people. 6 were parents. 1 guy thought it was a garage sale and stayed for the last 3 songs
worst show:
the power went out in the middle of Fractured Signal. it's in 7/8 so nobody knew when to stop. we played in the dark for 30 seconds. chad cheered anyway
dream venue:
the VFW hall. they have a stage, a real mic stand, and a sign that says NO DANCING. we'd respect the sign. we'd also be on a stage
favorite band:
jimmy eat world. also whatever my dad plays in the truck. don't tell the band
what's in ur guitar case:
2 picks, a tuner, a flashlight, 3 CD-Rs, and a fruit snack from 2 summers ago that has become part of the case
what do u eat before a show:
a blizzard. the employee discount is 1 per shift. best benefit in music
who do u want to open for:
anybody with a van
what's the dream:
somebody in the back singing along to a part and not knowing i can see them. that's it. that's the whole dream
describe ur band in one sentence:
6 songs, a card table, and a garage with great echo, and on a good friday that's everything
